title: GPT-6 Astra finds a counting proof of the Erdős–Sós tree-embedding conjecture
summary: A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The proof counts adjacency-marked vertex orderings and uses an induction on the tree to bound those not supporting a rooted copy. The exposition states the sharp classical theorem and records its proof was discovered by GPT-6 Astra; a Lean repository checks the benchmark formalization of the result. Related expository papers of the same proof are aliases, not separate discoveries.
ai_technology: Pre-release OpenAI GPT-6 Astra in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark
organization: OpenAI FrontierMath Erdős project; exposition by David R. Wood (affiliation not stated in arXiv record)

evidence.tested: A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv paper is an exposition of the proof, not the original benchmark output. The linked Lean proof is machine-checked against the benchmark formalization; the registry notes a minor parity-case difference in that compared statement, while the paper’s counting lemma derives the sharp classical average-degree threshold. This remains a preprint and the formalization is not independently audited here.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-6 Astra autonomously found the counting proof while solving Erdős problem 548 in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark; the exposition author reports the discovery and lays out the proof. A Lean 4 repository states the proof was machine-checked by a Comparator against the benchmark’s formal statement.
